newsitem.title: USA: Edison Intl earnings down on adjustments.
newsitem.headline: Edison Intl earnings down on adjustments.

text.p: Edison International Friday reported a decline in annual earnings -- to $716.7 million in 1996 from $739.1 million in 1995 -- saying per share impact was offset by the share repurchase program initiated in 1995.

On a per share basis, the company said earnings declined to $1.64 from $1.66. On an operating basis -- excluding one-time adjustments for Southern California Edison, Edison Mission Energy, and Mission Land Co -- earnings per share firmed to $1.70 from $1.69 a year earlier.

As part of a strategy to exit the real estate business and recover a substantial amount of cash invested in Mission Land's assets, the company said, it is executing a plan to sell most of the properties. As a result, the company took a real estate reserve in the fourth quarter.
Edison International noted its board has authorized the repurchase of up to $800 million in outstanding shares.

In 1996, the company said, it repurchased over 19.2 million shares for about $344 million. Since the inception of the program through December 31, 1996, over 23.4 million shares for have been repurchased for about $414 million.
The company said Edison Mission and Edison Capital contributed combined 1996 operating earnings of $0.29 per share, $0.06 higher than in the same period last year.

It said Edison Mission contributed a record high $92.1 million to net income in 1996 compared to $64.0 million in 1995 -- an increase of 44 percent primarily attributed to earnings from the newly acquired First Hydro project in the United Kingdom.
Edison Capital contributed a record $40.5 million to net income in 1996, up 3 percent from its prior earnings record of $39.5 million in 1995.
In 1996, Edison International said, it formed three new businesses: Edison Source, Edison EV (Electric Vehicles), and Edison Select (a consumer products and services company).

The company said expenses associated with the start-up of these new businesses, together with the parent company's interest payments on a $350-million debt issuance related to the acquisition of the First Hydro project, were responsible for a $0.05 per share decrease in 1996 operating earnings.
